q7.answer: The clients (PaymentsClient, EmailClient, GeocodingClient) hold a reference to the in-memory key cache, not a copy of the key, and each provider call reads the current value from the cache. A call that has already read a value keeps it, even if a refresh swaps in a new one mid-call. The cache is the only holder of the values.

q8.answer: The plan relies on two checks: Step 8 confirms all 4 pods run the v2 image digest and that each pod logged its version ids at startup, and Step 9 requires that no pod runs the v1 digest and no consumer uses key A. The plan does not define a live check of the key version each pod is using after later refreshes, so that confirmation is not fully decided.

q9.answer: The order is: (1) Step 2 sets store paths and access policy; (2) Step 3 writes dev values; (3) Step 4 builds the code change on a branch, including removing api_key from config/app.yaml, but nothing is deployed; (4) Step 5 creates key B at each provider and writes it to orders-api/prod/<name> while A stays active; (5) Step 6 merges and builds v2, which is when the committed-file removal reaches the image; (6) Step 7 rolls v2 out, which is when the app starts reading from the store; (7) Step 8 soaks; (8) Step 9 revokes key A at each provider, one at a time.

q10.answer: Local runs use dev values in orders-api/dev/* through the same loader, with make run setting APP_ENV=dev, and never use live keys; offline mode uses stub provider clients with no network or store access. How an engineer authenticates to the store for dev reads was never decided and is open question 3.

q11.answer: The plan treats any failed secret fetch the same way: it retries that fetch 3 times, 2 seconds apart, and if every attempt fails it logs the error without values and exits non-zero, so the pod never listens or becomes ready. The plan does not separately address a secret that is reported as not found versus one the store cannot serve, and it does not explicitly say whether the other two secrets are retried.
